title: State machine replication
summary: State machine replication (SMR) implements fault-tolerant services by running multiple deterministic state machine replicas and coordinating their inputs. Determinism ensures that identical inputs applied in the same order produce identical states and outputs across all non-faulty replicas. To tolerate F crash failures, 2F+1 replicas are required; Byzantine failures requiring cryptographic signatures need 3F+1 replicas. The critical operation is ordering inputs consistently across replicas, achievable via causal order when communication is fully visible, or consensus ordering when hidden channels exist. Outputs are generated by each replica and a majority-approved output is returned to clients; if no majority agrees, the response is FAIL. Failure detection compares replica states and outputs, restarting deviating replicas via checksums.

mechanisms.title: Input Ordering via Consensus
mechanisms.explanation: Inputs are ordered through a series of consensus instances, ensuring all non-faulty replicas process inputs in the same sequence. This consensus ordering guarantees consistent state and output across replicas despite failures or hidden communication channels.

mechanisms.title: Output Filtering and Client Response
mechanisms.explanation: Each replica independently processes inputs to generate outputs. Before replying to a client, faulty outputs are filtered out; typically a majority of replicas must agree on the same output. If no majority output exists, the system returns FAIL to the client.
